analyzed_vuln.description: In frame_get_metalayers_from_header, the metalayer content length (`content_len`) is read from attacker-controlled frame header bytes and used directly in `malloc((size_t)content_len)` and `memcpy(content, content_marker + 5, (size_t)content_len)` without validating that `content_len` is non-negative and that `offset + 1 + 4 + content_len <= header_len`. A negative `content_len` is cast to a huge size_t, causing invalid memcpy parameters (wild destination / overlap) and ASan memcpy-param-overlap crash at line 1173.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: The fuzz harness calls `blosc2_schunk_from_buffer(data, size, false)`, which parses untrusted in-memory frame bytes via `frame_to_schunk -> frame_get_metalayers -> frame_get_metalayers_from_header`. The input must pass basic marker checks (e.g., metalayer index marker 0xde, offset marker 0xd2, content marker 0xc6) and provide an in-range `offset`, but set the 32-bit `content_len` field to a negative value (or otherwise inconsistent large value). Because bounds checks use `header_pos += content_len` (can decrease on negative) and no direct range check on `content_len`, memcpy is invoked with a huge length and crashes.
